svg.title: Antibiotic resistance: selection and spread
svg.desc: A three-stage schematic shows pre-existing variation, antibiotic selection and reproduction of resistant survivors, with a conditional plasmid-conjugation route.
svg.text: Antibiotic resistance: selection and spread
Marlbridge • AQA GCSE Biology 8461 • Inheritance, variation and evolution (4.6.3)
ANTIBIOTIC TREATMENT SELECTS RESISTANT VARIANTS • IT DOES NOT DIRECT THE MUTATION
1 • VARIATION BEFORE TREATMENT
Mostly susceptible; a rare resistant variant may be present.
Variation can arise by mutation before exposure.
2 • ANTIBIOTIC EXPOSURE
Susceptible bacteria are reduced; resistant bacteria can survive.
Treatment changes survival; it is not a directed mutation.
3 • SURVIVORS REPRODUCE
The resistant variant can become more common in this population.
If treatment continues inappropriately, resistant
bacteria may spread through reproduction.
A POSSIBLE ADDITIONAL ROUTE • PLASMID CONJUGATION
donor with resistance plasmid
recipient bacterium
If a resistance gene is carried on a transferable plasmid, conjugation can pass it
between compatible bacteria. This route is conditional; not every resistance gene is plasmid-borne.
Schematic population model; not clinical advice and not a measured dataset.
